newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg to sell Frosted Flakes in China, India.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg to sell Frosted Flakes in China, India.

text.p: Kellogg Co said Tuesday it plans to offer its Kellogg's Frosted Flakes in China, India and Thailand.
It also plans to offer a chocolate-flavored version of Frosted Flakes in the United States.
Kellogg said its China operations on Wednesday will introduce "Tony's Flakes," in reference to the Tony the Tiger emblem for its Frosted Flakes product.
In Thailand, Frosted Flakes will be sold under the name "Kellogg's Corn Frosties" beginning March 25, when the company opens its new plant there.
In India, the brand will be launched later this year under the name "Kellogg's Frosties."
Kellogg said it believes China, Thailand and India offer long-term growth potential for the company.
In the United States, Kellogg next month will introduce "Kellogg's Cocoa Frosted Flakes."

"The leveraging of equity we have built in our key brands like Kellogg's Frosted Flakes and innovative new products introductions like Kellogg's Cocoa Frosted Flakes are strong components of our global marketing strategy as we lead the cereal category into the 21st century," Carlos Gutierrez, who heads global business development for Kellogg, said in a statement.
Kellogg's Frosted Flakes is the second best-selling cereal worldwide, following Kellogg's Corn Flakes, a company spokesman said. In the United States, Frosted Flakes is the largest selling brand.
Frosted Flakes is marketed in about 150 countries.
